# rigged-macbook-3d

> React + three.js component library: a genuinely rigged 3D MacBook (openable lid on a
> real hinge, video/image screen, studio lighting presets, optional zero-dependency
> scroll journey). Peer deps: react>=18, three>=0.160,
> @react-three/fiber>=8.18, @react-three/drei>=9.122.

Install: npm i rigged-macbook-3d three @react-three/fiber @react-three/drei
All components are client components (Next.js App Router: dynamic import, ssr:false).
The 3D model is bundled and fixed — never pass a different GLB to modelSrc.
Multiple <Macbook> instances per page are supported (each clones the node hierarchy on
mount; geometries/materials are shared across clones).

## Exports (from src/index.ts)

```ts
// --- Components ---

/** The rigged 3D MacBook. Headless and controlled: renders exactly the state its props
 * (or frameDriver) describe, inside any @react-three/fiber canvas. */
function Macbook(props: MacbookProps & React.RefAttributes<THREE.Group>): JSX.Element;

type MacbookProps = ThreeElements['group'] & {
  open?: number;               // 0=closed, 1=open. Linear. Default 1.
  screen?: ScreenInput;        // video URL, image URL, or ready THREE.Texture
  brightness?: number;         // 0=black, 1=full. Default 1.
  autoPlay?: boolean;          // default true; pauses the video while lid shut/dark
  modelSrc?: string;           // MUST be this package's assets/macbook-rigged.glb; other GLBs throw
  onLoad?: () => void;
  frameDriver?: () => MacbookFrameState; // per-frame override, read inside the render loop
};

interface MacbookFrameState {
  open?: number;
  brightness?: number;
}

/** Lighting rigs tuned for the Space-Black MacBook. */
function MacbookLighting(props: MacbookLightingProps): JSX.Element;

interface MacbookLightingProps {
  preset?: LightingPreset;  // 'studio-dark' | 'studio-light' | 'soft'. Default 'studio-dark'.
  intensity?: number;       // scales every light. Default 1.
  children?: ReactNode;     // if present, REPLACES the preset entirely
}

/** Wrapper div + <Canvas> with tuned camera (z 6, fov 32), ACES filmic tone mapping,
 * and a lighting preset. Drop a <Macbook> inside. */
function MacbookStage(props: MacbookStageProps): JSX.Element;

interface MacbookStageProps extends Omit<CanvasProps, 'children'> {
  lighting?: LightingPreset;       // default 'studio-dark'
  lightingIntensity?: number;      // default 1
  pauseWhenOffscreen?: boolean;    // default true; parks the frameloop off-screen
  className?: string;
  style?: CSSProperties;
  children: ReactNode;
}

/** The full scroll journey (pin -> lid open -> dive -> hold on the playing video ->
 * recede -> settle -> hand scroll back to the page), zero scroll-library dependencies. */
function MacbookScroll(props: MacbookScrollProps & React.RefAttributes<MacbookScrollHandle>): JSX.Element;

interface MacbookScrollProps {
  screen: string | ScreenSource;      // the video (or image) that plays once the lid opens
  height?: string;                    // default '600vh'
  lighting?: LightingPreset;          // default 'studio-dark'
  timeline?: Partial<Timeline>;       // unspecified beats keep tuned defaults
  poses?: PosesPartial;               // unspecified values keep tuned defaults
  feel?: Partial<Feel>;               // unspecified values keep tuned defaults
  pointerParallax?: boolean;          // default true
  fallback?: ReactNode;               // rendered instead of the journey if capability gate fails
  className?: string;
  modelSrc?: string;                  // see Macbook.modelSrc
  onProgress?: (p: number) => void;
  children?: ReactNode;               // overlay content above the canvas, inside the sticky viewport
}

interface MacbookScrollHandle {
  readonly progress: number;           // current smoothed journey progress, 0-1
}

// --- Hooks & utilities ---

function useScreenTexture(source?: ScreenInput): {
  textureRef: React.RefObject<THREE.Texture | null>;
  ready: boolean;
  setPlaying: (playing: boolean) => void;  // play/pause a video source; no-op otherwise
};

/** boolean | null (null on first render, SSR-safe). true iff WebGL2 is available and
 * prefers-reduced-motion is not set. Only ever downgrades true->false live. */
function useCapabilityGate(): boolean | null;

function journeyState(p: number, timeline: Timeline, poses: Poses): JourneyState;

interface JourneyState {
  deviceIn: number;   // 0-1 eased fade/rise-in
  open: number;        // 0-1 eased lid amount -> Macbook `open`
  brightness: number;  // 0-1 eased screen wake -> Macbook `brightness`
  pose: Pose;
}

function ramp(p: number, a: number, b: number): number;       // 0->1 across [a,b], clamped
function easeInOut(t: number): number;                        // cubic ease-in-out
function lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number): number;
function clamp01(v: number): number;
function smoothDamp(
  current: number, target: number, velRef: { current: number },
  smoothTime: number, dt: number, maxSpeed: number,
): number;                                                     // critically-damped follow (no overshoot)

const DEFAULT_MODEL_URL: string;   // versioned unpkg URL, pinned to installed package version
const DEFAULT_TIMELINE: Timeline;
const DEFAULT_POSES: Poses;
const DEFAULT_FEEL: Feel;
const LID: { OPEN_X: number; CLOSED_X: number };   // hinge angles, radians
const SEAT: { HINGE_Y: number; HINGE_Z: number; SCREEN_BOTTOM_Y: number; SCREEN_BOTTOM_Z: number; TARGET_Y: number };
const FIT_SIZE: number;            // world size (max dimension) the model is normalised to

function resolveTimeline(t?: Partial<Timeline>): Timeline;    // merges over DEFAULT_TIMELINE
function resolvePoses(p?: PosesPartial): Poses;               // per-pose deep merge over DEFAULT_POSES
function resolveFeel(f?: Partial<Feel>): Feel;                // merges over DEFAULT_FEEL

// --- Types ---

type ScreenInput = string | ScreenSource | THREE.Texture;
interface ScreenSource {
  src: string;
  type?: 'video' | 'image';   // forces kind when the extension is ambiguous
  fallbackSrc?: string;       // tried if `src` fails to load/decode
}

interface Timeline {
  deviceIn: [number, number];  // device fades/rises in
  lidOpen: [number, number];  // lid closed -> open; screen wakes across the back 80%
  dive: [number, number];     // camera-relative: intro pose -> dived-in pose
  recede: [number, number];   // push-back so the whole laptop is visible again
  // Two deliberate rests: the gap between dive[1] and recede[0] is the hold (the
  // open MacBook plays its video front and centre while the user keeps scrolling),
  // and the tail between recede[1] and 1 is the settle (the pushed-back device
  // rests a beat before the pin releases and the page scrolls on).
}

interface Pose { yaw: number; pitch: number; scale: number; x: number; y: number; }
interface Poses {
  intro: Pose;
  dive: Pose;
  outro: { scale: number; y: number }; // pure scale/level change; rotation held from dive pose
}
interface PosesPartial {
  intro?: Partial<Pose>;
  dive?: Partial<Pose>;
  outro?: Partial<{ scale: number; y: number }>;
}

interface Feel {
  smoothTime: number;        // seconds; follow time of the damped scrub. Higher = floatier.
  maxSpeed: number;          // progress/second cap so a full-page fling stays fluid
}

type LightingPreset = 'studio-dark' | 'studio-light' | 'soft';
```

## Canonical snippet 1: static stage

```tsx
import { Macbook, MacbookStage } from 'rigged-macbook-3d';

export default function Hero() {
  return (
    <div style={{ height: 600 }}>
      <MacbookStage lighting="studio-dark">
        <Macbook open={1} screen="/demo.mp4" />
      </MacbookStage>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Canonical snippet 2: scroll journey

```tsx
import { MacbookScroll } from 'rigged-macbook-3d';

export default function Journey() {
  return (
    <MacbookScroll
      height="600vh"
      screen={{ src: '/videos/demo.webm', fallbackSrc: '/videos/demo.mp4' }}
      fallback={<div>Here's a quiet fallback instead.</div>}
    />
  );
}
```

The pinned journey: the device rises in closed, the lid opens onto the playing video, the
camera dives in and holds there while the user keeps scrolling, then the device recedes,
settles for a beat, and the page scrolls on. Lengthen the hold by moving `timeline.recede`
later, or give the whole journey more scroll room with `height`. Keep the settle generous
(the default leaves 0.87–1): the damped follow trails raw scroll, so the pushback needs that
runway to finish and rest before the pin releases.

## Canonical snippet 3: frameDriver binding (e.g. Framer Motion)

```tsx
import { Macbook, MacbookStage } from 'rigged-macbook-3d';
import { useMotionValue, animate } from 'framer-motion';

export default function HoverOpen() {
  const openMV = useMotionValue(0);
  return (
    <div onPointerEnter={() => animate(openMV, 1, { type: 'spring', stiffness: 120, damping: 20 })}
         onPointerLeave={() => animate(openMV, 0, { type: 'spring', stiffness: 120, damping: 20 })}>
      <MacbookStage>
        <Macbook screen="/demo.mp4" frameDriver={() => ({ open: openMV.get() })} />
      </MacbookStage>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## DEFAULT_TIMELINE, DEFAULT_POSES, DEFAULT_FEEL (as JSON)

```json
{
  "DEFAULT_TIMELINE": {
    "deviceIn": [0, 0.18],
    "lidOpen": [0.24, 0.48],
    "dive": [0.42, 0.64],
    "recede": [0.74, 0.87]
  },
  "DEFAULT_POSES": {
    "intro": { "yaw": -0.5, "pitch": 0.32, "scale": 0.62, "x": 0, "y": 0.25 },
    "dive": { "yaw": 0, "pitch": 0.05, "scale": 1.0, "x": 0, "y": 0.05 },
    "outro": { "scale": 0.68, "y": 0.05 }
  },
  "DEFAULT_FEEL": {
    "smoothTime": 0.45,
    "maxSpeed": 0.5
  }
}
```

## The fallback / capability gate

`useCapabilityGate()` returns `null` on the first render (SSR-safe), then `true` or `false`.
It is `true` only if the browser supports WebGL2 (`three` r163+ requires it) AND the user has
not set `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. It re-evaluates live on a media-query change listener,
but only ever downgrades `true -> false` — it never re-upgrades mid-session, because remounting
a 3D scene under a user who is already looking at the fallback is its own kind of motion.

`<MacbookScroll>` consumes this directly: while `capable === null` it renders an empty
height-holding placeholder (`<div style={{ height }} />`) so layout doesn't jump; once resolved,
it renders either the full journey (`capable === true`) or the `fallback` prop's content
(`capable === false`). If you compose `<Macbook>`/`<MacbookStage>` yourself outside of
`<MacbookScroll>`, call `useCapabilityGate()` yourself and branch the same way. Always give
`fallback` meaningful non-3D content (a screenshot, a short description, a recorded video) —
never an empty element — since a real fraction of visitors will see it.
